title: Ratatouille. Remy the cooking rat.
lines: In the country of France there is a big, beautiful city.
In Paris there is a very tall tower made of iron.
In the evening it sparkles with thousands of lights.
There are bridges over the river, cosy little streets and lots of restaurants where you can eat delicious food.
But our story doesn't start in Paris.
It starts in a little house in the countryside.
A family of rats lives in the attic.
One of those rats, a little grey one with big ears, is called Remy.
Remy is different from the other rats.
Rubbish, old peels and dirty things from the bin.
Remy has a super good nose.
He knows exactly which food is tasty and which food is yucky.
He tastes a piece of cheese.
And then a piece of strawberry.
And then cheese and strawberry together.
Then he sees all sorts of colours and hears music in his head.
Remy wants to be only one thing.
He wants to be a real chef!
A cook in a big restaurant, with a white apron and a tall white hat.
His big hero is the famous chef Gusteau.
Gusteau wrote a book, and it says: Anyone can cook!
The old lady who lives in the house sees the rats.
He gets washed away, through dark tunnels.
And when he finally climbs up and looks out of a skylight, what does he see?
And right in front of him is Gusteau's restaurant.
Remy looks through the kitchen window.
Linguini is tall and thin and a bit clumsy.
He scrubs the pots and pans.
But Linguini accidentally spills something into the soup.
And the soup becomes completely yucky.
He adds a bit of this, a bit of that, some herbs, some salt.
Everyone in the restaurant thinks it's the tastiest soup ever.
But they think Linguini made it!
But then they have an idea.
Remy can cook, and Linguini can't.
Linguini can work in the kitchen, and Remy can't.
Remy hides under Linguini's tall white chef's hat!
There he sits, on Linguini's head, hidden under the hat.
When Remy pulls on the right side, Linguini's right arm goes up.
When he pulls on the left side, the left arm goes up.
That's how Remy steers him, like a puppet!
Together they chop vegetables, super fine and super fast.
It becomes the tastiest food in all of Paris.
But then the strictest food critic in France comes.
He is tall and thin, and he never laughs.
When he says a restaurant is bad, nobody comes anymore.
Remy knows what he has to make.
In thin slices, nicely laid out in a circle.
He puts it in front of Anton Ego.
Because it tastes exactly like the ratatouille his mummy used to make, when he was a little boy.
Then Anton Ego wants to see the chef.
But Anton Ego says: Anyone can cook.
And from then on Remy has his own restaurant in Paris, with a view of the Eiffel Tower.
He wears a little white chef's hat.
And he is the best chef in all of France.
